leftEvidence.role: The baptism becomes a public question
leftEvidence.title: The risen Jesus commissions baptism among all nations

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus claims all authority and sends the eleven to make disciples of all nations.
points.right: The risen Jesus teaches about God’s Kingdom and tells the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for the Father’s promise.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Baptizing and teaching are joined to the threefold name and the promise of Jesus’ presence.
points.right: He recalls John’s water baptism and announces baptism in the Holy Spirit after a few days.

payload.posture: Matthew and Acts place baptism language in risen-Jesus commissions.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus contrasts John’s water baptism with the Spirit promise

payload.tension: Matthew commands an ongoing disciple-making practice; Acts announces an imminent divine act.
payload.title: Baptizing nations and waiting for Spirit baptism
